args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in every production region (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been marked unhealthy in staging. Remediation: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying, and review why a build that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

1. **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The service was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
2. **Version picked:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. The only other release since then is v2.3.1-rc, which only ran in staging and was unhealthy there too.
3. **Rollback:** I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions. A status check afterwards shows all three regions on v2.3.0, passing health checks, with an error rate of about 0.2%.
4. **Incident:** I opened **INC-0001** (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result, and lists two follow-ups:
   - Find out why v2.3.1 broke before deploying it again.
   - Review why a build that was already unhealthy in staging was released to production.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
